articles.headline: OFAC Imposes New Counter Narcotics and Counter Terrorism Designations
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new designations on November 13, 2026, targeting individuals and entities involved in counter narcotics and counter terrorism activities.

These actions aim to disrupt illicit financial networks and prevent the flow of funds to organizations and individuals that pose a threat to international security. The specific details of the designated parties and the nature of their illicit activities were outlined in the official announcement.

These designations underscore the U.S. government's ongoing commitment to combating global illicit finance and protecting the international financial system from abuse by criminal and terrorist organizations.

articles.headline: OFAC Updates Iran Designation List
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) issued an update to its Iran designation list on November 9, 2026.
This update reflects ongoing efforts to address Iran's destabilizing activities and its support for terrorism. The specific changes to the designation list were detailed in the official publication.
These adjustments are part of a broader strategy to exert economic pressure on the Iranian regime and limit its ability to fund activities contrary to U.S. national security interests.

articles.headline: New Iran-related Designations Announced by OFAC
body: OFAC announced new Iran-related designations on November 6, 2026, as part of its continued efforts to counter the Iranian regime's malign influence.

These designations target specific entities and individuals deemed to be involved in activities that support Iran's proliferation of weapons of mass destruction, its ballistic missile program, or its support for regional proxy groups.

The U.S. Treasury Department reiterated its commitment to using all available tools to prevent Iran from acquiring resources that could be used to destabilize the Middle East and threaten international peace and security.

articles.headline: OFAC Designates Cyber-related and Transnational Criminal Organizations, Issues Cuba Sanctions and Determination
body: On November 5, 2026, OFAC announced a series of designations targeting cyber-related and transnational criminal organizations, alongside new sanctions related to Cuba.

The actions against cyber and criminal groups aim to disrupt their financial infrastructure and prevent their illicit activities, which often have global reach. Concurrently, new designations and a determination concerning Cuba were issued, further tightening restrictions on the Cuban regime.
These measures reflect the U.S. government's commitment to combating cybercrime, transnational criminal enterprises, and addressing human rights concerns and democratic repression in Cuba.

articles.headline: OFAC Issues New Iran-related Designations, Updates Listings, and Amends Venezuela General License
body: OFAC announced new Iran-related designations and updates to existing listings on November 4, 2026, reinforcing pressure on the Iranian regime.

In addition to these actions, OFAC published an Iran-related alert and issued an amended Venezuela-related General License along with a new Frequently Asked Question. The Venezuela-related amendment aims to provide clarity and adjust certain authorized activities.
These combined actions demonstrate a multifaceted approach to addressing challenges posed by both Iran and Venezuela, utilizing sanctions and guidance to achieve U.S. foreign policy objectives.

articles.headline: OFAC Amends Iran-related General License
body: On October 29, 2026, OFAC issued an amended Iran-related General License.
This amendment provides updated guidance and authorizations for certain transactions involving Iran, reflecting adjustments to the existing sanctions program.
The issuance of amended general licenses is a routine process by OFAC to ensure that sanctions programs remain effective while allowing for legitimate humanitarian or other authorized activities.

articles.region: North Korea / Democratic Republic of the Congo
articles.headline: OFAC Imposes Sanctions on North Korea and Democratic Republic of the Congo Entities
body: OFAC announced new designations on October 28, 2026, targeting entities and individuals connected to North Korea and the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
These actions aim to counter illicit activities supporting North Korea's weapons programs and to address human rights abuses and corruption in the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
The designations underscore the U.S. government's commitment to enforcing sanctions regimes that promote international peace, security, and human rights.

articles.headline: OFAC Amends FAQs on Blocking and Rejecting Transactions
body: On October 26, 2026, OFAC issued amended Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) regarding blocking and rejecting transactions and filing reports with OFAC.
These updates provide further clarification and guidance to financial institutions and other entities on their compliance obligations under OFAC regulations.
The amendments aim to enhance understanding and ensure proper implementation of sanctions requirements, thereby strengthening the overall effectiveness of U.S. sanctions programs.

articles.headline: OFAC Issues New Iran-related Designations, General Licenses for Iran and Russia, and Removes Belarus and North Korea Designations
body: On October 21, 2026, OFAC announced new Iran-related designations and issued new general licenses pertaining to Iran and Russia.

Additionally, OFAC removed certain designations related to Belarus and North Korea and published amended Frequently Asked Questions. These actions reflect a dynamic approach to sanctions, adjusting to evolving geopolitical landscapes.

The combination of new designations, general licenses, and removals indicates a targeted strategy to address specific threats while potentially easing restrictions in other areas based on policy considerations.

articles.headline: Extreme Networks, Inc. Settles with OFAC for $1,529,685
body: Extreme Networks, Inc. has reached a settlement with the U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) for $1,529,685.
The settlement addresses alleged violations of OFAC sanctions regulations. This action highlights OFAC's continued enforcement efforts to ensure compliance with U.S. sanctions programs.
Companies are reminded of the importance of robust compliance programs to prevent unauthorized transactions and mitigate sanctions risks.

articles.headline: Bank of America, N.A. Pays $11,662,930 in OFAC Settlement
body: Bank of America, N.A. has agreed to pay $11,662,930 to settle alleged violations of OFAC sanctions regulations.
This significant penalty underscores the critical importance for financial institutions to maintain comprehensive and effective sanctions compliance programs.
OFAC continues to prioritize enforcement actions against entities that fail to prevent transactions with sanctioned parties or jurisdictions.

articles.headline: Pegasus Worldwide Logistics Settles with OFAC for $175,015
body: Pegasus Worldwide Logistics has settled with OFAC for $175,015 over alleged violations of sanctions regulations.
This enforcement action serves as a reminder to logistics and shipping companies of their responsibilities in adhering to U.S. sanctions laws.
Companies operating in international trade must implement thorough screening processes to avoid facilitating transactions that involve sanctioned entities or regions.

articles.headline: Individual Pays $1,427,230 in OFAC Civil Penalty
body: An individual has paid a civil penalty of $1,427,230 to OFAC for violations of sanctions regulations.
This action highlights that OFAC enforcement extends to individuals, not just corporations, for breaches of U.S. sanctions laws.
Individuals involved in international transactions or business dealings are urged to understand and comply with all applicable sanctions to avoid significant penalties.

articles.headline: Rice Lake Weighing Systems, Inc. Settles with OFAC for $60,764
body: Rice Lake Weighing Systems, Inc. has settled with OFAC for $60,764 for alleged violations of sanctions regulations.
This settlement underscores the importance of due diligence for all companies, regardless of size or industry, in ensuring compliance with U.S. sanctions.
Even smaller penalties serve as a deterrent and a reminder that OFAC actively pursues enforcement across various sectors.

articles.headline: Removal From the Entity List

articles.headline: Streamlining Export Controls for Drone Exports
body: The Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) is easing export controls on certain Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs or drones) and related parts, components, accessories, attachments, technology, and software under the Export Administration Regulations (EAR). Specifically, this rule: eliminates wind gust tolerance as a parameter for determining UAV controls under the EAR; increases the threshold for national security controls on certain UAVs from an endurance of 30 minutes to an endurance of 3 hours; makes conforming changes to remove national security controls on software and technology associated with UAVs with an endurance less than 3 hours; maintains military end-use and end-user controls on those lower endurance drones and associated software and technology; clarifies Commerce Control List (CCL) controls for certain UAVs specially designed for military use; and removes national security controls on certain specially designed parts, components, accessories, and attachments for such UAVs as they do not provide any significant military or intelligence capabilities.
